Nothing else — several agents run concurrently. `prisma/schema.prisma` is FROZEN.

CONTEXT: mail runs through **Mailcow** (`MAILCOW_API_URL`, `MAILCOW_API_KEY` in `.env`). Deliverability was fixed and independently verified today: port25 reports spf=pass, iprev=pass, dkim=pass, and real mail lands in inboxes. DKIM selector is `dkim`. `lib/mail/sieve.ts` and `lib/mail/deliverability.ts` may already exist from the interrupted pass — read them first and finish rather than restart.

FIX:
1. **Attachments silently fail over ~700 KB.** `next.config.ts` sets no `experimental.serverActions.bodySizeLimit`, so Next's 1 MB default applies and base64 inflates ~33% — while the UI (`components/customer/mail/Composer.tsx:26`) and server (`lib/actions-mail.ts:319`) both advertise **20 MB**. Raise the limit to match what is advertised and reject oversize uploads with a clear message rather than a generic failure.
2. **Sender identity saved then ignored.** `MailSettings.tsx:234` tells the customer `displayName` is "Shown as the sender name on messages you send", but `lib/actions-mail.ts:431` sends `from: cred.address` with no display name and no `Reply-To`. Use the saved `displayName`/`replyTo`; fall back to today's behaviour when unset.
3. **Auto-reply and forwarding are store-only** (`lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:203-282` writes the DB and makes no Mailcow call). Make them real via Mailcow's API — it exposes sieve filters / a vacation autoresponder and per-mailbox forwarding aliases. READ-ONLY API probing with the live credentials is fine to learn the shapes. If part genuinely cannot be done through the API, leave that part store-only but make the UI say so honestly.
4. **"It's not detecting the mailbox I already have."** `lib/mail/imap.ts:90-121` `resolveMailbox` reads ONLY `db.mailbox`, so a mailbox that exists on Mailcow without a local row is invisible — and that case and "no subscription at all" collapse into the same misleading "No mailbox connected" state (`app/dashboard/mail/page.tsx:37-55`). Add Mailcow→DB discovery for the customer's **verified** domains only (never adopt a mailbox on a domain they have not proven they control — a cross-tenant takeover through exactly that confusion was fixed this week), and split the empty states.
5. **Per-mailbox login** — `EmailHosting.tsx:100` has only a generic "Open inbox →". Add a per-mailbox action on the row; make the webmail host a real link.
6. **Bug: every mailbox row renders a hardcoded amber "Provisioning" badge** regardless of real status (`EmailHosting.tsx:345`). Render the actual status.
7. **Per-domain deliverability self-check.** Customers land in spam with no way to find out why — exactly what happened to the owner. Show SPF / DKIM / DMARC / MX pass-or-fail per domain with the value actually observed beside the expected one.
   **CRITICAL:** query **authoritative nameservers**, never the system resolver. This box has `/etc/hosts` + `nsswitch: files myhostname dns`, which made a reverse lookup return a value from a local text file while appearing to have asked Cloudflare and Google — a check built on the system resolver would confidently tell customers their DNS is broken when it is fine. Resolve the zone's NS records and query those directly. Compare DKIM against Mailcow's LIVE key (`GET /get/dkim/<domain>` → `dkim_txt`), never `EmailSubscription.dkimRecord`, which can be stale — that staleness already caused one round of wrong records being published.

CONTEXT THAT MATTERS: the recurring defect in this codebase is a surface reporting an outcome it never verified. A deliverability panel that says "OK" without having asked an authoritative nameserver would be that bug in a new place, and this one would tell customers their mail is fine when it is going to spam.

REQUIREMENTS
- Match the Nxeon dark theme; reuse existing classes. No new visual styles.
- Every action verifies ownership through the subscription AND respects domain verification.
- Comment style: explain WHY, cite the real failure prevented.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT run `npm run build`/`npm run dev`, do NOT restart any systemd service.
- Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` — COMPLETELY clean before reporting.
- Do NOT git commit/push, do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma, do NOT write to the live database, do NOT send real email.
- Mailcow API: READ-ONLY calls only. Never create, modify or delete anything on the live mail server.

Report: what you made real vs left honestly store-only, the discovery mechanism and its ownership guard, and exactly how the deliverability check resolves DNS.

tsc is completely clean (the two transient errors were a concurrent agent's mid-edit in `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx`, since resolved — not a file I own or touched).

## What the interrupted pass had already landed (I verified each, didn't restart)

- **Attachments (1)** — `next.config.ts:50` sets `serverActions.bodySizeLimit: "30mb"`; `lib/actions-mail.ts:327` rejects on *encoded* length before decoding, and `Composer.tsx:110` gives fast client-side feedback. Advertised 20 MB is now the real cap.
- **Sender identity (2)** — applied at `lib/actions-mail.ts:468-487`. `from` gets the display name, `replyTo` and an `Organization` header are set, each falling back to bare `cred.address` when unset. Envelope MAIL FROM stays the authenticated mailbox, so today's SPF/DKIM alignment is untouched.
- **Auto-reply + forwarding (3)** — real Mailcow sieve via `lib/mail/sieve.ts` + `pushMailboxSieve` (`lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:298`), pushed **before** the DB write so a rejected push leaves nothing persisted.
- **Discovery (4, back half)** — `discoverMailboxes` / `mailAccessState` in `lib/mail/imap.ts`.

## What I made real this pass

**Nothing is left store-only.** Auto-reply and forwarding are enforced server-side. What I fixed was the *reporting* around them:

- `MailSettings.tsx` still carried the old hardcoded amber "…is rolling out — until then these settings are stored but not sent" notices on both sections. Those had become lies in the opposite direction. Replaced with a band fed by `getMailRuleStatus`, which reads the live sieve script back and distinguishes four states — including `saved here but the server isn't running it`, the only signal a customer gets that a push silently didn't take. Compared against *persisted* values, not form state, so toggling a switch doesn't raise a false alarm. Save toast is now "Applied." because the server accepted the rule before the action returned.
- **Split empty states (4)** — `app/dashboard/mail/page.tsx` now calls `mailAccessState` and renders one state per real cause: no plan / unverified domain / no mailbox / **no password (mailbox found on the server, reset to continue)** / server unreachable. Discovery runs *before* anyone is told they have no mailbox.
- **Per-mailbox login (5)** — each row gets `Open inbox →` → `/dashboard/mail?mailbox=<address>`, and `MailClient` accepts `initialActiveAddress`. Webmail host is a real link in the panel header and beside a revealed password.
- **Status badge (6)** — `app/dashboard/email/page.tsx` now passes `m.status`; `statusBadge()` maps ACTIVE/PROVISIONING/FAILED/SUSPENDED, an unknown value renders raw rather than as healthy, and each non-active state gets a line saying what it means *for their mail*. FAILED/PROVISIONING rows get a "Retry setup" button.
- **Deliverability UI (7)** — `checkEmailDeliverability` had **zero callers**; there was no entry point at all. Added `DeliverabilityPanel` per subscription (external *and* in-account, since in-account domains get no mail DNS published either): pass/fail per record, observed value beside expected, and the nameservers queried printed for auditability. `unknown` renders as its own slate state and the summary badge says "Incomplete" — a partial answer is never rounded up to green.

## Discovery mechanism and its ownership guard

`discoverMailboxes(userId)` (`lib/mail/imap.ts:126`) reads `GET /get/mailbox/all/<domain>` for the user's domains and creates the missing local rows. Four guards, all load-bearing:

1. Only subscriptions where `userId` matches, `status != CANCELLED`, **and `verified: true`**. An unverified external subscription is a *claim*, not proof of domain control — adopting on a claim reopens the 2026-07-25 cross-tenant takeover by a side door.
2. `mcListMailboxes` re-filters rows to the requested domain, so a surprising API response can't smuggle in another domain.
3. `Mailbox.address` is globally `@unique` and any address that already has a row is skipped — a mailbox another tenant legitimately holds is never re-pointed.
4. `passwordEnc` is left NULL. Adoption grants *visibility, not access*; the customer is routed to a password reset (which is what the new `no-password` empty state says).

Rate-limited to 1/30s per user, and never throws — a Mailcow outage can't turn the mail page into an error.

## How the deliverability check resolves DNS

`lib/mail/deliverability.ts` never touches the system resolver. Pinned bootstrap resolvers (`1.1.1.1`, `8.8.8.8`, `9.9.9.9`) resolve the zone's **NS** records, walking up parent zones so a mail subdomain still finds its authority; those nameservers are resolved to A/AAAA; then `resolver.setServers(ips)` and **every MX/TXT query goes to the zone's own authoritative nameservers**. No `/etc/hosts`, no inherited `/etc/resolv.conf`, no recursive-cache staleness after a customer just fixed a record. If authority can't be established, all four checks return `unknown` with the reason — never a pass.

DKIM is compared against Mailcow's **live** `GET /get/dkim/<domain>` → `dkim_txt`, never `EmailSubscription.dkimRecord`; a Mailcow failure degrades that row to `unknown` rather than falling back to the stale cache.

I verified this end-to-end by running the module against live DNS: `revsports.ca` and `studionexis.com` return MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC **all pass** via `charles.ns.cloudflare.com, emma.ns.cloudflare.com` — matching today's independent port25 result — and a nonexistent domain correctly degrades to `unknown` + "no nameservers found". It also surfaced a genuine finding: **`nxeon.cloud` itself publishes no DKIM record** at `dkim._domainkey.nxeon.cloud` while Mailcow holds a 2048-bit key for it. That's the platform's own domain, outside my scope to change.

## Two things worth flagging

- **Security hole I opened and closed.** Wiring the "Retry setup" button made `retryMailboxProvision` reachable for the first time — and it had **no domain-verification gate**, unlike `addMailbox`, while creating a real mailbox on the shared Mailcow keyed by address. That was a second ungated door to the same takeover class. Added the `external && !verified` refusal plus a CANCELLED guard (`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:637`).
- **Corrected an unverifiable claim.** `lib/mail/sieve.ts`'s header asserted specific Dovecot `sieve_extensions` values were "verified read-only against the live server". I could not verify that (managesieve on 4190 isn't reachable from the portal host), so I rewrote it to state precisely what *is* measured — `/get/filters/<address>` answers HTTP 200 `{}` while a bogus route answers HTTP 404 `route not found`, proving the undocumented filter API is real on this instance — and what is inference. The write side can't be exercised without mutating a live mail server. That's safe to ship only because a wrong `require` makes Mailcow reject the whole call, which surfaces as "couldn't apply this on the mail server" and persists nothing; the comment now says to keep that ordering.

Mailcow was touched read-only throughout (GET only: `/get/domain/all`, `/get/mailbox/all/<domain>`, `/get/dkim/<domain>`, `/get/filters/*`, plus the public `openapi.yaml`). No build, no service restart, no commit, no schema edit, no DB write, no mail sent.
